hints.junior: The cart total is wrong and a dozen files emit cart:update — any of them could be the culprit, none are visibly connected in the code.
hints.mid: emit and on for the same event name can live in files that never import each other, so grepping the string is the debugging tool, not the type system.
hints.staff: This is structural to pub-sub: subscribing is a runtime relationship with no compile-time trace, by design, not a bug in this particular bus.

hints.junior: Same stale-total bug, two ways to find it — toggle and see how much searching each one takes.
hints.mid: The props version isn't faster because the code is shorter, it's faster because there's exactly one place the value could have come from.
hints.staff: Notice the props version doesn't have "eleven emitters" as a category of bug at all, a value can only be set from the one place allowed to set it.

hints.junior: With props, finding where a value comes from means following a variable, not grepping a string across the whole codebase.
hints.mid: Prop drilling costs typing. An event bus costs traceability. Neither is free, the question is which your team can afford for this state.
hints.staff: The real middle ground is colocated state via context for one clear owner, reserving a bus for things that are genuinely cross-cutting and ownerless.

hints.junior: If prop drilling hurts, reach for context first, it still has one traceable source, it just skips the manual passing.
hints.mid: Ask before adding to a bus: can you name the one component that should own this state? If yes, it belongs in a store, not the bus.
hints.staff: Keep a typed event map and a discoverable emitter/listener registry for any bus event that survives — bound the debugging cost, don't eliminate it and hope.

sections.junior: Hey! Today's case is about a cart total that's wrong, and a dozen files that could all be the reason, thanks to a global event bus.
sections.mid: An event bus decouples the sender from needing to know who's listening — emit and on calls for the same event can live in files that never import each other, so grepping the event string is the only debugging tool.
sections.staff: This is a structural property of pub-sub, not a bug in this particular bus — subscribing to an event is, by design, a runtime relationship with no compile-time trace.

sections.junior: With props, finding a bug means following a variable to its source. With a bus, it means grepping every file that might emit that event name.
sections.mid: Prop drilling costs you typing, passing a value through layers that don't use it. An event bus costs you traceability, since any listener could be the source with no static path from emitter to listener.
sections.staff: The middle ground most codebases want is colocated state via context for anything genuinely shared across a subtree, reserving a global bus for things that are legitimately cross-cutting and don't belong to any one owner.

sections.junior: Toggle between the event bus version and the props version, and see what it actually takes to trace the same bug in each.
sections.mid: Both versions have the same bug — a stale coupon calculation overwrites a fresh shipping calculation. The difference is entirely in how much you have to search to find it.
sections.staff: The props version doesn't have "eleven emitters" as a category of problem at all — a value can only be set from the one place that's allowed to set it.

sections.junior: Before you put state on a shared event bus, ask whether one component should really own it. If so, pass it as a prop instead.
sections.mid: Before putting state on a bus, ask if one component should own it. If yes, use props or context with a single write path, not a bus.
sections.staff: Reserve a global bus for genuinely cross-cutting concerns with no single owner.
